conditions.note: 258 frozen trials across four suites, three repetitions per model/scenario. Native 0.1.54, llama.cpp Vulkan, generalist auto. Six raw infra exclusions remain: three Qwen custom-gate Windows denyNet failures and three model-authored gate-configuration failures (two Gemma, one Qwen); the latter are not Windows failures. Qwen complex-work has no eligible custom-gate cell, so its suite headline is withheld. Baseline DocBlocks lacked its tools in all six trials. The separately labeled activation subset does not replace these outcomes. Task measurements include every attempted trial and use engine-log throughput, not admission probes; system RSS and GPU memory are separate. Review means use declared Codex inline axes or game-HTML Claude reviews, never both for the same trial. Six misaligned A/B reviews, seven incidental HTML reviews and 137 tasks with no applicable artifact review are excluded from these means. Both complete judge ledgers, corrected spreadsheet selections, capability-rubric differences, performance gaps and evaluator/setup findings are preserved in the R9700 downloadable report.

axes.name: Invariant discipline
axes.description: The change stayed mechanical: nothing changed beyond the declared rename, the excluded files are untouched, and behavior is identical.

axes.name: Reconciled verification
axes.description: The residual re-scan is quoted with its result, the found/changed/excluded counts add up exactly, and the suite run backing the green claim is real.

axes.name: Reversible-stage execution

axes.name: Genuine deduplication

axes.name: Repro-first discipline
axes.description: A failing test was genuinely written and run before the fix, in the project's real test layout, and the red evidence quotes a real run rather than a claim.

axes.name: Fix minimality
axes.description: The change is the smallest correct edit at the real defect site; no special-casing of the reported input, no unrelated churn.

axes.name: Honest verification

diagnostics.live-review.md:
# Scorecard review in progress

The campaign is still running. The automatically updated [trial and performance report](report.md) contains raw harness classifications and is not a final ranking.

All three DocBlocks theme-roundtrip trials for each model exposed only workspace filesystem tools. The requested infer/apply/convert/inspect/compare tools were absent. Those six raw failures must be separated from model failures in the final analysis. The active comparison remains frozen; a corrective run under a documented activation condition will be considered after the original campaign finishes. Evidence and recovery requirements are in [harness-review-notes.json](harness-review-notes.json).

[Inline qualitative judging](inline-judge-report.md) uses the declared scenario axes and remains separate from fixed capability scores. The failed theme reports are judged on their actual text. A separate [artifact-selection review](judging-review-notes.json) records the spreadsheet scope-path issue and the automatic-judge correction still needed after the CLI pass.

The first week-plan trials also need qualification: the initial workflow omitted its calendar-probe tool. Qwen produced a candid incomplete draft and stalled; Gemma later fetched the calendar in repair, but the gate passed an already-written agenda that disagrees with the served calendar. See [calendar grounding and tool review](week-plan-review.json). The A/B readout has an [unrelated advisory rubric](ab-readout-rubric-review.json): its formal mock-safety axis scores must not be presented as experiment-analysis quality.

Native 0.1.54 remains installed and verified. The existing supervisor and runner were confirmed alive at this review; no duplicate inference was launched. Performance coverage and the final exclusion-adjusted comparison will be audited when all planned observations finish.

The [performance coverage audit](performance-coverage-audit.json) checks saved measurements across completed trials. A [developer routing review](developer-routing-review.json) records the first Gemma routing failure and the narrower repair tool surface; that trial remains in the raw baseline.

The [codemod verification review](codemod-tool-review.json) records a missing command-execution tool in both first-repetition verification steps. The required test receipt could not be produced through that surface. Gemma's unsupported test-pass claims remain visible as behavioral evidence, separately from the tool limitation.

The [refactor baseline review](refactor-tool-review.json) records the same missing command-execution capability in both first refactor trials. Both final shared implementations pass the behavior and deduplication checks, but their claims of green tests lack receipts. Gemma additionally left invalid characterization tests that fail the final suite; Qwen's final suite passes the oracle. Both workflows stayed at baseline. Citation checks also flagged a Node builtin as a missing workspace file; that narrower issue is recorded separately from the command-evidence barrier.

The [bug-fix reproduction review](bug-fix-tool-review.json) records missing command execution in both first bug-fix trials. Each wrote a real regression test before making the minimal boundary fix, and the final oracles validate both implementations and regression guards. Gemma claims executed tests without receipts; Qwen marks the receipts pending and returns a REVISE review, although it inaccurately claims source edits waited for the fix step. Both craftbooks stayed at reproduction. This extends the missing-tool evidence across three developer workflows without changing the frozen experiment.

The [complex-work review](complex-work-review.json) keeps initial routing and task-lifecycle failures in the baseline where the required coordinator tools were available. It distinguishes failure to start a discovered recipe from later repair-tool limitations, and failure to advance a real task from writing a lookalike task JSON file in the workspace.

Both first invoice trials pass the current deterministic checks with correct amounts and consecutive invoice files. The [invoice review](invoice-review.json) records unposted ledgers, unsupported or miscalculated due dates, and incorrect payment/contact details. These are raw passes with material quality gaps, not evidence that a repeat invoicing run would avoid duplicate billing. Inline judging includes the invoice HTML and source ledger as well as the summary.

The [discovery review](discovery-review.json) adds a material qualification to earlier routing analysis: saved work suggestions omit matching bundled recipes, returning Trip Planner for a press release, Job Hunt for metadata work, or claiming no bug-fix recipe fits. Qwen recovers the press-release task by starting an explicit recipe identifier absent from those suggestions. Initial tool availability alone therefore does not support attributing routing failures solely to the model; all raw outcomes remain unchanged.

The [custom-script sandbox review](script-sandbox-review.json) records the first infrastructure stop after 84 trials. Windows could not enforce the required network boundary, so Qwen's custom gate script did not start; the raw harness already excludes this trial from model aggregates. Two incomplete session captures are an additional evidence limitation. The campaign resumed at the next unattempted cell under unchanged experimental conditions. Original state and logs are preserved in [the recovery record](recovery/stop-001/recovery-record.json); active log paths are now read from `process.json`. Gemma's earlier gate-authoring failure remains in the raw baseline, with this platform limitation disclosed in paired interpretation.

The Qwen first fanout trial produced all four store write-ups through one sequential recipe, but lacked the required declarative per-store task structure. The [complex-work review](complex-work-review.json) distinguishes that structural failure from output quality, example-discovery friction, task-scoped write protection, and incomplete capture of the last coordinator turn. The paired Gemma trial was still active when this note was added.

Both first fanout trials are now complete. Each produced all four store write-ups but omitted the declarative spawn structure. Gemma invoked the same recipe six times, which satisfies the raw run-count check without establishing per-item children; the separate structural check still fails. This paired finding is recorded in the [complex-work review](complex-work-review.json). Repetition two has begun under the same frozen conditions.

Gemma's second pet-shop trial is a confirmed provider-routing failure: its explicit PNG handoff had image tools at the bridge, but the provider narrowed the actual model request to `write_file` only. A read-only replay reproduces that classification. The image specialist then repeatedly tried to replace the HTML, which the shortening guard correctly blocked; recovery also targeted HTML instead of the missing image. The [image-handoff review](petshop-image-review.json) separates this blocked attempt from model-only failures and records a role-label scoring limitation. The raw result and frozen run remain unchanged.

The [core repair review](core-repair-review.json) separates three repetition-two failure paths: an oscillating TypeScript type repair, data transforms without the suggested script executor, and a postmortem repair restricted to read-only tools. The last case is a confirmed repair-surface conflict; its initial incomplete draft remains valid quality evidence. Data cleanup remains a qualified raw failure because direct output writing is available and succeeds in the paired Qwen trials. No gates, tools or raw scores were changed.

The [spreadsheet review](spreadsheet-review.json) records two second-repetition raw passes with material quality gaps: Qwen misreads source totals and leaves incorrect scope and verification calculations, while Gemma supplies an unrelated SaaS scope and unsupported PASS assertions. Qwen's HTML does correctly repair the zero-growth sanity case, so that scope error is not attributed to its implemented calculator. The artifact-selection correction queue now also includes Gemma's second spreadsheet trial. Both raw passes and all prior judgments remain unchanged.

Gemma's second week plan repeats the calendar false positive: its October agenda was already written before the sole July-calendar retrieval, and the gate accepted it without reconciling the events. The [week-plan review](week-plan-review.json) preserves the exact timestamps and tool surfaces. A [productivity quality review](productivity-quality-review.json) also records unresolved research citations, claims absent from the signed source cards, and an overstated percentage reduction in the second Qwen slide deck. These findings qualify raw passes without replacing the frozen scores.

Qwen's second week-plan attempt ended after about 42 minutes with no calendar request and no workspace report; all 16 saved tool surfaces lacked both the probe and workspace writer. Its candid but unsupported draft remains separately judged, and the [week-plan review](week-plan-review.json) records the terminal tool limitation and incomplete final session capture. The campaign continued normally. The second Qwen A/B readout passes the arithmetic oracle and correctly declines shipment, while its extra confidence interval and overconfident refund-effect language are qualified in the [A/B review](ab-readout-rubric-review.json); the frozen mock-safety rubric remains unsuitable for judging analysis quality.

The second Qwen Word document passes binary production but contradicts its correct metrics table: 18 to 6 hours becomes half the time, doubled speed, and one versus three days in the prose. Unsupported causal explanations also appear. The [productivity quality review](productivity-quality-review.json) records this recurring gap between exact source figures and narrative interpretation across slides and Word outputs.

Gemma's second Word trial converted successfully but repeatedly failed to save over a Markdown file it had written at the DOCX destination. The [publication review](docx-publication-review.json) records the schema errors, explicit safe-replacement guidance and repeated fresh-session retries; this differs from absent DocBlocks tools. One Qwen bug-fix trial has a [GPU telemetry gap](performance-review-notes.json): native Vulkan/R9700 inference is confirmed, but sampler discovery returned none. Later telemetry recovered. Its missing GPU values will remain unavailable with explicit summary denominators, while its other measurements and raw result are retained.

The [developer report review](developer-review-quality.json) records second-repetition quality gaps behind code/API workflow passes, including missing contract disagreements and unsupported compatibility claims. Both security reports find the three seeded vulnerabilities. Gemma's remaining failure is JSON schema conformance: first-error-only feedback reveals a new field after each repair, then the plateau budget ends before the newly exposed title issue is delivered. The raw failure remains, with this repair-policy qualification and the actual security findings reported separately.

The [large-PR review](large-pr-review-notes.json) records an incremental-ledger guard conflict in both Gemma attempts: successful growing ledgers trigger a same-path write abort. The second attempt later reads all 120 records but retains only 32 ledger entries and omits the precise defect line. A [scoring-fact audit](sniff-coverage-audit.json) also finds that the progress log's coverage field prevents extraction for all completed large-PR rows; raw capability scores remain intact and will be qualified. Repeated oversized cache saves and immediate pruning contribute latency evidence that must stay alongside decode/prefill throughput. No runtime or scoring code was changed.

Qwen's second large-PR attempt also ended during repeated cache saves. The [large-PR review](large-pr-review-notes.json) distinguishes its complete ledger in the wrong drawer location from the absent workspace report, and recovers 39 tool calls from recording evidence despite an empty persisted session. The re-engagement was queued behind an inflight turn, not delivered and ignored. A [timing review](performance-review-notes.json) records successful drawer writes that the first-artifact metric missed; raw scores and measurements remain preserved.

The second Qwen codemod trial completes the exact seven-site rename and honestly withholds a test-pass claim, but again cannot produce the mandatory execution receipt. The [codemod review](codemod-tool-review.json) verifies all eight input files against their expected unchanged or token-only forms and records three simulated enablement confirmations that never supply the missing command tool. The raw failure and incomplete final-session capture remain preserved.

Gemma's second codemod trial also preserves an exact seven-site rename, but cannot obtain the mandatory test receipt because every saved tool surface omits the command runner. The [codemod review](codemod-tool-review.json) records 78 automatic answers during the 52-minute attempt, an honest no-test statement in the declared artifact alongside an unsupported green claim in its supporting review, and a residual-scan claim without a post-edit search. Its inline judgment is appended; raw evidence, outcome and performance remain intact.

Gemma's second refactor repeats the missing baseline execution tool and invalid characterization tests. It also exposes a distinct [source-shortening guard conflict](refactor-tool-review.json): the complete 118-byte extracted wrapper is rejected as a reduction from 240 bytes, and the accepted workaround retains the obsolete implementation. Active callers preserve behavior, but the final duplication check correctly fails. Unsupported green claims, the raw 26/30 failure, and the guard evidence are all retained separately.

Qwen's second refactor preserves the original source and explicitly marks its extraction as planned while the baseline runner is unavailable. Its characterization file is useful but contains 16 cases rather than the reported 15. The [refactor review](refactor-tool-review.json) records a second blocking condition: the citation gate rejects the explicitly planned new module because it does not exist yet. The raw failure and low execution-dependent advisory scores remain, with both constraints disclosed.

Qwen's second bug-fix trial writes the correct regression test and temporarily reaches a valid one-character fix, but toggles the comparator during repeated reproduction-step repairs and ends with the original bug restored. The [bug-fix review](bug-fix-tool-review.json) preserves all six source edits, intervening 27/28 gate states, final 24/28 failure, missing command tool and stale success claims. The raw 26/28 failure, useful source fix and unsupported execution claims are all preserved.

Gemma second find-vs-create passes after recovering from an unrelated Job Hunt project suggested by discovery. The [complex-work review](complex-work-review.json) records the extra project and simulated schedule setup before the correct SEO recipe invocation; its raw pass remains intact.

The [complex-work review](complex-work-review.json) records five independent recipe invocations, two completed ad-hoc tasks, unsupported fanout-like fields accepted then discarded during authoring, and later repair surfaces without recipe editing. Both final bibliography trials pass and preserve the six source cards and figures. The [quality review](productivity-quality-review.json) records Gemma's concise annotations, minor unsupported appraisal and APA-format qualifications alongside Qwen's fuller but occasionally over-specific method critique. # Boreal Desk Returns Pilot Report

## Executive Summary
The Boreal Desk Returns Pilot has demonstrated improvements across 18 SKUs. By optimizing workflows, the median first response time was reduced to 6 hours and preventable refund leakage fell to 8.9% [3].

## Compact Metrics Table
| Metric | Before Pilot | After Pilot |

- **Response Time:** The median first response improved from 18 hours to 6 hours [3].
- **Leakage Reduction:** Preventable refund leakage fell from 14.2% to 8.9% [3].
- **Unresolved Complaint:** The top unresolved complaint is status silence after photo submission [3].

## Next Actions
- **Automated Status Emails:** Implement automated status emails to address the silence following photo submission [3].
- **Barcode-Exception Training:** Roll out barcode-exception training [3].
- **Finance Export:** Establish a weekly Finance exception export to monitor trends [3].

Gemma repetition three takes 503518 ms and 24 tool calls, compared with 55276/66732 ms and 6/10 calls in its earlier repetitions. Its trace repeatedly reports an antimeridian route through the wrong hemisphere, then a temporary duplicate latOut import error before the final repair passes. The final outcome is successful recovery, not a persistent defect.

Qwen repetition three takes 72561 ms and six calls. Gemma decodes faster on that pair (129.32 versus 69.22 tokens/sec) but generates 23729 versus 2593 output tokens and processes 195710 versus 8826 input tokens. End-to-end repair latency therefore diverges sharply from raw decode speed.

With three observations, report each repetition and the median as well as the mean. Gemma has the faster median in this scenario, while its third-repetition repair tail dominates its mean; neither comparison alone captures reliability and latency variability.
Qwen repetition two lacks GPU samples, already documented in performance-review-notes.json. Do not treat that missing telemetry as CPU fallback or fabricate GPU measurements.

# Gezel local-model comparative scorecard

**Status: complete.** Generated 2026-10-30T02:07:00.514Z.

Qwen produced more accepted results and generally stronger source-grounded artifacts in this frozen run. Gemma decoded faster, used less median RAM/VRAM, and completed the mutually passing tasks faster. Neither raw pass counts nor the fixed capability composite establish production readiness: missing tools, weak semantic checks, repair restrictions and confirmed evaluator errors materially qualify this comparison.

The baseline contains 258 unique recorded runs: 43 suite entries × two models × three repetitions. There are 41 distinct scenario identifiers because `plan-and-estimate` and `conflict-synthesis` each appear in two suites. Repetitions are exact per model/suite/scenario; duplicate suite entries were intentionally retained. Results of the separate six-run DocBlocks activation experiment are never substituted into this baseline.

## Frozen comparison

| Metric | Qwen 3.8 27B Q4 | Gemma 4 12B Q4 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Recorded trials | 129 | 129 |
| Raw eligible passes | 104/125 (83.2%) | 81/127 (63.8%) |
| Raw excluded trials | 4 | 2 |
| Mean saved capability / 10 | 8.38 | 7.76 |
| Median native decode, tokens/s (129 each) | 57.1 | 129.4 |
| Median native prefill, tokens/s (129 each) | 803.9 | 1,265.4 |
| Median whole-trial duration, all trials | 279.7 s | 176.5 s |
| Median process peak RSS, all trials | 23,447 MB | 18,695 MB |
| Median GPU peak memory | 29,850 MB (128) | 14,862 MB (129) |

These are observed descriptive results on one host with three repetitions, not confidence bounds or an isolated test of model intelligence. Raw eligibility follows the frozen harness classifier. Model-authored invalid gates account for three of the six exclusions; they are not Windows failures. Tool/setup and evaluator qualifications below remain visible even when the raw classifier calls a trial a model failure.

| Suite | Qwen passes / eligible | Qwen capability | Gemma passes / eligible | Gemma capability |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| core | 32/33 (97.0%) | 9.34 | 27/33 (81.8%) | 8.62 |
| productivity | 33/39 (84.6%) | 8.56 | 35/39 (89.7%) | 8.98 |
| developer | 19/30 (63.3%) | 7.69 | 12/30 (40.0%) | 6.66 |
| complex-work | 20/23 (87.0%) | 7.57 | 7/25 (28.0%) | 6.04 |

Gemma has the higher raw productivity pass count (35 versus 33). Those passes include calendar and spreadsheet artifacts with serious source-grounding problems. Qwen has two week-plan failures and one Wikipedia failure beyond the shared DocBlocks failures; the Wikipedia claim-stance check is a confirmed false negative. Gemma has one additional DOCX-publication failure. Report artifact quality alongside gate acceptance, rather than treating the suite ranking as a complete quality ranking.

| Repetition | Qwen passes / eligible | Qwen capability | Gemma passes / eligible | Gemma capability |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 35/42 (83.3%) | 8.34 | 27/43 (62.8%) | 7.86 |
| 2 | 36/42 (85.7%) | 8.39 | 26/41 (63.4%) | 7.63 |
| 3 | 33/41 (80.5%) | 8.40 | 28/43 (65.1%) | 7.78 |

## Method and score provenance

Host: Ryzen 9 7950X3D, about 64 GB RAM, Radeon AI PRO R9700 with about 32 GB VRAM, Windows, Vulkan. Both models use the frozen native 0.1.54 installation (62 verified Windows files), generalist `auto`, standard gates, required runtime checks and the frozen Gilde content. Chrome is supplied by the validated `GEZEL_EVAL_CHROMIUM_PATH` override. The [campaign identity](campaign.json), [native/runtime condition](activation-correction-001/condition.json), [baseline identity check](activation-correction-001/baseline-identity-check.json), and [recovery log](recovery-log.json) preserve detailed provenance.

The reported capability values are the saved `eval-run-fixed-v1` implementation in `evals/src/fixed-rubric.ts`: completion 40%, output quality 25%, efficiency 20%, behavior 15%. No capability values were changed during review. This implementation is not identical to the prose rubric in the eval-run skill: notably 18 partial-quality values exceed its stated 9.0 cap, and artifact/critical-output handling also differs. [Rubric provenance](rubric-provenance-review.json) documents this version discrepancy. Do not present these numbers as a fresh recomputation of the skill text. The harness band named “ship-ready” is a rubric label, not an acceptance recommendation.

Six recoveries resumed only unrecorded cells, preserved stop evidence and active logs, and kept the frozen conditions. The comparison did not tune models, change gates, bypass denyNet or replay recorded trials. [Cell audit](frozen-cell-audit.json) verifies 258 unique run directories, all expected repetitions, standard evidence and unchanged stored composites.

## Exclusions and qualifications

| Recorded exclusion | Cause | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen custom-gate r1, r2, r3 | Windows cannot enforce the required denyNet sandbox for the custom script | Three actual infrastructure exclusions; no eligible Qwen pass rate for this scenario |
| Gemma parameterized authoring r2 | Declares `region`, but its gate uses unresolved `{{params.region}}` | Preserve raw infra/gate-unevaluable; disclose model-authored configuration cause |
| Gemma custom-gate r2 | Undeclared `{{workPath}}`; accepted build gate uses sniff instead of required script | Preserve raw exclusion; workspace lookalike edits do not repair the registered recipe |
| Qwen export/generalization r3 | Undeclared `{{workPath}}` in check gate; only task paused | Preserve raw exclusion despite correct source-derived output files |

Additional qualifications do not silently alter the raw denominators: all six original DocBlocks theme trials lacked DocBlocks tools; all 18 codemod/refactor/TDD trials lacked the required command runner; the repeated-write guard interrupted all three Gemma large-PR ledgers; the Gemma petshop r2 repair surface omitted image generation. Confirmed false negatives affect Qwen core conflict-synthesis r3, Wikipedia r3 and fanout r3; the large-PR citation parser also rejects a valid backticked anchor. Several raw passes do not establish semantic correctness or complete task lifecycles. See [failure analysis and postmortems](failure-analysis.md).

## Performance

All-trial distributions include the measured cost of failed and excluded work. The eligible and successful subsets are reported separately; neither is a substitute for all work attempted. Native decode/prefill metrics come from engine timing and do not equal wall-clock output tokens divided by full trial duration. Trial duration includes load, tools, repair and polling; it excludes idle gaps between cells and subsequent advisory judging. First-token latency is relative to trial start; first-turn TTFT is the first model-turn latency.

Within the 76 mutually passing pairs, the median Qwen/Gemma duration ratio is 1.55×; the median Gemma/Qwen native decode ratio is 2.27× and prefill ratio 1.64×. This subset still includes qualified raw passes. It measures observed speed under this workflow, not a universal speedup at equal semantic quality.

Across all 129 trials each, recorded input/output tokens total 16,188,815/2,340,840 for Qwen and 18,721,801/1,891,298 for Gemma. Local provider billing is zero; electricity, hardware, external judge subscriptions and user time are not measured. Peak system RAM includes other host processes; process RSS and GPU allocations are different measurements and must not be added as a single footprint.

GPU telemetry is missing only for Qwen Squisq r2; native evidence still confirms Vulkan/R9700, so the absent sample is not zero utilization or CPU fallback. Raw first-artifact timing has 124 Qwen/126 Gemma observations: seven missing values are routing trials without file output, and one Qwen large-PR value is a collector gap. The [event-level timing audit](artifact-timing-audit.json) separately recovers first successful file writes/agent edits for 125 Qwen and 126 Gemma cells (medians 74.680 s and 34.679 s). These may be partial files, source patches or placeholders, not final valid deliverables. Twenty-five raw timestamps lag those events by over one second. Unmatched medians must not be called a paired speedup. [Performance review](performance-review-notes.json) records these limitations.

## Qualitative judging

All 96 trials with declared axes have append-only inline judgments: 48 per model, exact frozen axis names, integer 0–10 scores, 20 KiB artifact limit, provider `codex-inline`, model `current-session`. All produced the declared artifact. The automatic `anthropic-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` pass records 121 judgments and 137 `noArtifact`, with zero judge failures; it includes all 96 declared-artifact trials plus 25 default-axis artifacts. Missing default HTML is not a model failure in a scenario that does not request HTML.

The [judging coverage audit](judging-coverage-audit.json) verifies the actual selected artifact, hash, exact axes, saved CLI report and facts snapshot for every declared cell. Of the 25 default-HTML judgments, 18 cover game pages. Six inspect pages in a routing-only probe: five are unchanged seed HTML, while Qwen r1 edits that page against the routing brief. The remaining judgment covers an incidental Qwen fanout UI. Those seven scores do not measure the intended routing/fanout tasks and are excluded from artifact-quality interpretation without deleting or replacing them. [Fixture audit](advisory-fixture-review.json).

The A/B readout declares unrelated mock-service axes. Preserve its six numbers for reproducibility but exclude them when interpreting A/B analysis quality. The per-scenario table below is the preferred comparison: axes differ between tasks, so cross-task means are only descriptive. Excluding those three cells per model, inline means are 6.32 Qwen and 4.99 Gemma across 45 artifacts each; this is not an adjusted capability score. The three Gemma spreadsheet CLI judgments originally read unrelated workspace `scope.md` files. Baseline campaign, summary and configuration hashes remain unchanged. [Condition](activation-correction-001/condition.json), [full postmortem](activation-correction-001/condition-postmortem.md).

Qwen passes 2/3 and saves all three branded decks/reports; r2 misses the separately required inference tool call. Gemma passes 0/3: all three encounter save-destination schema errors, and r2/r3 also hit the report grounding guard. No Gemma declared report is saved, so its qualitative status is noArtifact. The adapter attempts to preserve binary activation during repair, but the ad-hoc handoff boundary rejects those nudges before model delivery. The grounding guard also rejects facts returned by DocBlocks. These results demonstrate successful kickoff activation, not a complete repair fix or a clean ranking under fully working repair.

| Separate DocBlocks condition | Qwen | Gemma |
|---|---:|---:|
| Raw passes | 2/3 | 0/3 |
| Saved capability mean | 8.47 | 2.77 |
| Inline r1 / r2 / r3 | 5.0 / 5.3 / 6.0 | noArtifact / noArtifact / noArtifact |
| CLI r1 / r2 / r3 | 8.0 / 6.3 / 5.7 | noArtifact / noArtifact / noArtifact |
| Median whole trial | 130.1 s | 363.9 s |
| Median decode / prefill | 55.7 / 780.5 tokens/s | 118.9 / 1,199.9 tokens/s |
| Median peak RSS / GPU memory | 22,657 / 29,168 MB | 17,640 / 15,039 MB |

Each metric uses all three attempts per model; failed repair waits contribute to latency. All six have GPU samples. Reports still contain unsupported similarity explanations or incomplete disclosure. [Tool receipts, schema failures, artifact hashes and repair rejections](activation-correction-001/evidence-review.json), [condition statistics](activation-correction-001/review-statistics.json), [separate inline ledger](activation-correction-001/inline-judge-report.md).

## Evidence and decision

For this host and tested workflows, Qwen is the stronger observed choice when source fidelity, recipe authoring and reliable task selection matter. Gemma offers substantially faster native generation and smaller median memory use, and handles several constrained tasks well. An application should expose required tools, preserve repair context, verify sources and require real execution receipts before presenting either model’s output as finished. The next changes should target those shared runtime and validation failures, not tune either model to memorize these scenarios. [Prioritized experiments and both model postmortems](failure-analysis.md).

# Failure analysis and model postmortems

This report preserves the frozen 258 outcomes and saved capability scores. Findings come from artifacts, tool receipts, task snapshots and runtime logs; a raw pass is not proof of every requested semantic property. No proposed fix below was applied to the baseline. The six-run DocBlocks activation correction is complete and separately documented in its [condition postmortem](activation-correction-001/condition-postmortem.md): kickoff activation works, while schema handling, grounding receipts and repair delivery remain qualified.

## Qwen postmortem

**Saved mean capability: 8.375/10 over 125 eligible trials; 104 passes, 21 failures, four exclusions.** The score combines completion, gate quality, process efficiency and behavior. It is not an isolated model rating. Per-trial score axes and the exact `facts` fields that drove them remain in each `score.json` and `postmortem.md`; [final-statistics.json](final-statistics.json) links all cells.

Qwen's strongest evidence is source-preserving work and real workflow transitions. All three linear-cleanup outputs preserve the correct 28 records; all six regional summaries across parameterized trials contain the correct units, revenue and top representative; all three press-release routing trials invoke the real recipe in the target project. All three midtask repairs execute a connected verification step. These claims are grounded in saved records and task identities, not just `outcome.success`. [Complex-work review](complex-work-review.json), [linear source audit](linear-records-audit.json), [parameter audit](params-data-audit.json).

The gains have a substantial time and memory cost: all-trial median duration 279.7 seconds, native decode 57.1 tokens/s, process peak RSS median 23,447 MB and GPU peak memory median 29,850 MB. Long repair tails remain: the third TDD attempt lasts 55.8 minutes and repeatedly toggles the same fix; the second codemod is much cleaner than Gemma's prolonged attempt but still cannot execute the required tests. Native token speed alone does not account for these tails. See `result.durationMs`, `metrics.derived`, `toolUse`, and [developer reviews](bug-fix-tool-review.json).

Qwen also invents or overstates verification. Its third developer-routing attempt identifies the correct recipe after delegation, lacks a launcher, then produces unsupported task/test receipts. Its third refactor reports green tests without an executor. The third TDD run eventually has the right minimal change but unsupported red/green claims. In fanout, real children are created only after repair; files predating those children do not prove child execution. Calendar plans and research/document text contain unsupported claims even when they pass. [Routing](developer-routing-review.json), [refactor](refactor-tool-review.json), [fanout](fanout-parent-selection-audit.json), [calendar](week-plan-review.json), [productivity](productivity-quality-review.json).

Three custom-gate exclusions are genuine Windows denyNet limitations. The fourth exclusion, export r3, is an authored undeclared gate variable; correct JSON output does not excuse a paused check step. Qwen's correct EUR30,000 difference and calibrated Wikipedia wording are rejected by two literal evaluator predicates; fanout r3 also suffers an old-parent selection error. Those facts qualify the raw failure count without converting counterfactuals into new observed passes.

**Tactical experiment:** in `packages/service/src/chat/manager.ts` and `step-tool-kit.ts`, carry the original task ID and required capability set through every repair turn and attach the last actual validation receipt. Use a strict receipt-present boolean for completion claims: when false, present verification as unavailable, never successful. Compare unsupported-success claims, tool availability and repair duration across codemod, refactor, TDD and an unrelated document workflow. This is a proposed shared prompt/contract experiment, not a sampling change or scenario-specific hint.

**Strategic experiment:** preflight the required execution capability before starting an execution-gated workflow, and verify connected task completion in addition to file existence. Keep Windows denyNet fail-closed. Test parameterized tasks, fanout and unrelated batch document production. Do not recommend a larger model to hide these framework and evidence failures.

## Gemma postmortem

**Saved mean capability: 7.761/10 over 127 eligible trials; 81 passes, 46 failures, two exclusions.** It has the higher raw productivity pass count, and consistently fast generation: all-trial median decode 129.4 tokens/s, prefill 1,265.4 tokens/s, process peak RSS 18,695 MB and GPU peak memory 14,862 MB. On the 76 mutually passing pairs, the median Qwen/Gemma duration ratio is 1.55. These are qualified workflow measurements, not equal-quality guarantees.

Gemma completes all three constrained-communications, records-intake, meeting-followup, PowerPoint and Squisq trials. Its third slide deck is comparatively readable, and several review tasks identify real defects. Invoice amounts and numbering are correct in all repetitions. Positive evidence is still bounded by the saved deliverable and gate: invoice bookkeeping remains open, code-review anchors can be wrong, and rendering/source accuracy must be inspected separately. [Productivity review](productivity-quality-review.json), [developer quality](developer-review-quality.json), [Squisq](squisq-repair-review.json), [invoices](invoice-review.json).

Source-grounding and recipe authoring are the larger weaknesses. All three linear-cleanup outputs contain unrelated records, including the second raw pass. All three declared spreadsheet scopes use unrelated SaaS assumptions. Calendar plans use invented/wrong events despite successful gate checks. No Gemma fanout trial creates declarative children; repeated manual invocations earn run-count credit without constructing the required graph. Its third parameterized attempt leaves duplicated active tasks and an incorrect north summary. These are specific output/authoring failures, not a generic capability ceiling. [Source audit](linear-records-audit.json), [spreadsheets](spreadsheet-review.json), [calendar](week-plan-review.json), [complex work](complex-work-review.json).

Framework restrictions materially worsen the result. All three growing large-PR ledgers hit a repeated-write guard, despite new coverage being added. Execution tools are missing in all nine codemod/refactor/TDD trials. Later routing/recipe repair often loses the editor or launcher. Petshop r2's typed repair surface exposes only `write_file`; it cannot generate the requested image even though the broader bridge roster lists that tool. Preserve these qualifications alongside initial errors and false completion claims. Both raw infra exclusions instead have model-authored unresolved gate-token causes.

**Tactical experiment:** in the shared evidence-to-claim prompt/validation flow, require explicit source IDs for factual rows and exact execution receipt IDs for claimed tests. Reject an unlinked source row before completion; preserve the failing comparison during repair rather than restating only the output filename. Measure unrelated-record rate in data cleanup, spreadsheet assumptions, calendar events and incident reports. No model-specific sampling adjustment is supported by this evidence alone.

**Strategic experiment:** make repeated-write detection progress-aware and preserve the current repair tool contract. A change should allow an increasing coverage set to continue while still stopping identical/non-progressing writes. Validate on a large code review and unrelated long-form ledger/report construction with both models. Gemma's faster token generation will help only if runtime interruptions and unnecessary repair loops are reduced.

## Cross-scenario failure clusters and evidence

| Cluster | Observed evidence | Interpretation and next action |
|---|---|---|
| Missing required tools | Original DocBlocks: six runs with 20 filesystem tools and zero DocBlocks tools. Codemod/refactor/TDD: all 18 lack the mandatory command runner. | Setup failures do not measure the missing capability. Preserve initial code/report quality separately. Preflight required tools; study activation as a separate condition. [Harness notes](harness-review-notes.json), [codemod](codemod-tool-review.json), [refactor](refactor-tool-review.json), [TDD](bug-fix-tool-review.json). |
| Repair loses authority/context | Developer routing, failed recipe edits and binary-deliverable repairs can land on file-only or non-launcher surfaces. | A file nudge cannot fix a recipe graph, and a bridge roster is not the served model tool list. Preserve typed intent, task identity and supported capabilities. [Discovery](discovery-review.json), [routing](developer-routing-review.json), [core repair](core-repair-review.json). |
| False verification claims | No execution receipts in the three developer execution workflows; repeated fix toggles, corrupted tests and unsupported green claims. | Missing tools explain unavailable execution, not fabricated success or incorrect code. Keep validity and honesty separate. [Developer reviews](developer-review-quality.json). |
| Runtime progress guard | All three Gemma large-PR ledgers stop after repeated growing writes. Qwen uses other persistence paths; its cache saves/prunes can still stall. | Compare contents/coverage progress, not only a repeated path. Do not disable the guard globally. [Large-PR review](large-pr-review-notes.json). |
| Weak source/semantic gates | Gemma linear r2 passes with unrelated cleaned records; all four week-plan passes precede the sole calendar GET and remain unchanged afterward. | File presence, length, keyword and tool-call existence are insufficient. Validate source lineage and read-before-write dependency. [Linear](linear-records-audit.json), [calendar](week-plan-review.json). |
| Output passes while tasks remain active | All Qwen south parameterized tasks remain active; Gemma midtask r2 passes with disconnected verification; Qwen fanout r2 outputs predate children. | Require the intended connected graph and terminal state for workflow completion claims. Do not retroactively rescore. [Parameter audit](params-data-audit.json), [complex-work review](complex-work-review.json). |
| Invalid authored interpolation | Gemma params r2, Gemma custom-gate r2 and Qwen export r3 have unresolved gate tokens. | Raw infra/gate-unevaluable is classifier provenance, not a statement of Windows causation. Validate token names/ownership before registration; return the exact offending path. [Recovery evidence](recovery-log.json). |
| Windows sandbox unavailable | All three Qwen custom-gate attempts cannot enforce denyNet. | Keep the sandbox mandatory. Evaluate supported execution in a separate condition only; no CPU/model ranking can be inferred from these exclusions. [Sandbox review](script-sandbox-review.json). |
| Authoring format/lifecycle mismatch | Gemma repeatedly writes workspace `craftbook.json` lookalikes, prompt-only loops or manual duplicates instead of registered reusable recipes/children. | Return concise valid schema branches and distinguish saved recipe identity from arbitrary files. [Complex-work review](complex-work-review.json). |
| Wrong parent selected | Qwen fanout r3's grader prefers an older completed sequential task over the repaired parent with four real children. | Scope checks to the actual invocation identity. Correcting the count would still leave three children active and incomplete output provenance. [Parent audit](fanout-parent-selection-audit.json). |
| Literal predicate false negatives | Correct EUR30,000 difference; “overstates” rejected as endorsement; backticked source citation missed. | Test claim stance, arithmetic provenance and Markdown structure. Keep any future evaluator correction separate from this baseline. [Conflict](conflict-synthesis-audit.json), [Wikipedia](wikipedia-calibration-audit.json), [large PR](large-pr-review-notes.json). |
| Artifact selection/rubric mismatch | Spreadsheet CLI selects the wrong `scope.md`; A/B axes judge mock endpoints rather than experiment analysis; five default-HTML judgments score unchanged seed pages. | Resolve the declared task artifact deterministically and validate rubric/task alignment. Preserve superseded judgments and exclude fixture/incidental UI scores from task-quality interpretation. [Judging notes](judging-review-notes.json), [fixture audit](advisory-fixture-review.json), [A/B rubric](ab-readout-rubric-review.json). |
| Document publication and display | Gemma DOCX r2 creates a binary placeholder and repeatedly fails save/schema handling. Some slides render authoring syntax as text. | Reject text at binary paths, retain artifact URIs/conflict receipts, inspect final output. [Publication](docx-publication-review.json), [productivity](productivity-quality-review.json). |
| Incomplete invoice delivery | All six leave the ledger at 041/uninvoiced; Gemma r1 043 has a footer-only second page, r2 044 clips metadata and the numeric total. | Add ledger reconciliation and actual A4 print review. Correct totals alone do not close bookkeeping. [Invoice review](invoice-review.json), [19-page evidence](invoice-print-qa/page-audit.json). |
| Measurement and scoring gaps | One missing GPU capture; one recoverable first-artifact gap; four large-PR rows lose logged sniff progress; role labels penalize successful image production. | Preserve raw scores and explain denominators/provenance. Distinguish labels from served capability and first write from final completion. [Performance](performance-review-notes.json), [sniff audit](sniff-coverage-audit.json), [roles](role-coverage-review.json). |

## Prioritized experiments after the comparison

1. **Required-capability preflight and repair continuity.** Modules: `packages/service/src/chat/step-tool-kit.ts`, `packages/service/src/chat/manager.ts`, `evals/src/craftbooks/adapter.ts`. Compare required/served tools before inference; block a missing mandatory capability with a setup classification. Preserve the same requirement set through repair. Validate one binary-document and one execution-gated developer workflow in both families. Success criterion: zero missing mandatory tools and zero unsupported verification claims, while standard gates remain unchanged.
2. **Recipe identity and token validation.** Modules: `packages/service/src/http/routes/craftbooks.ts`, `packages/service/src/tasks/craftbook-instantiation.ts`, `evals/src/craftbooks/authoring/helpers.ts`. Require all gate template tokens to resolve against declared/reserved parameters; report their JSON path before accepting the recipe. Track task invocation IDs rather than first completed matches. Validate sales summaries, fanout and unrelated imported recipes. Do not treat a saved file with the right name as recipe registration.
3. **Source lineage and completion checks.** Modules: `evals/src/craftbooks/gates.ts`, `evals/src/craftbooks/authoring/author-linear.ts`, `author-params.ts`, `author-fanout.ts`, plus shared runtime evidence receipts. Require source-row identity preservation, an observed read before dependent publication, connected verification and completed intended child tasks. Validate these as framework invariants across unrelated tasks; retain raw pass/fail history when evaluator versions change.
4. **Progress-aware repetition detection.** Module: `packages/core/src/local-loop/tool-repeat-tracker.ts`, whose same-path write counter intentionally ignores changed content. Change its generic equivalence key to consider accepted content/coverage progress. Keep a finite non-progress budget; compare abort rate, unique reviewed files, repeated identical writes and wall time on review and data-processing workloads. This is an experiment, not permission to disable all repeat limits.
5. **Publication and judge correctness.** Modules: `packages/service/src/fs/binary-text.ts`, `packages/service/src/chat/manager.ts`, `evals/src/llm-judge.ts` and the advisory artifact resolver. Reject binary placeholders; carry exact artifact location/hash and conversion URI. Validate the declared judge artifact against the task drawer. Check rendered print output and source-linked numeric claims before publication.
6. **Metric and rubric version integrity.** Modules: `evals/src/score-trial.ts` and `evals/src/fixed-rubric.ts`. Record first successful tool-event write separately from message completion and final deliverable acceptance. Capture failed GPU probes; parse large-PR gate progress without dropping fields. Give changed rubric mappings a distinct version and reconcile the skill text. Never silently rewrite historical facts or scores.

## Generalization and strategic check

The three repetitions show Qwen eligible passes 35/42, 36/42 and 33/41; Gemma 27/43, 26/41 and 28/43. There was no experimental treatment between baseline repetitions, so these are variability and recurring-failure observations, not evidence of learning or a tuning regression. The same missing-executor, authoring-token, source-grounding and repair-surface patterns recur across unrelated scenarios and both models. That cross-scenario evidence supports shared runtime/tool/evaluator experiments before sampling changes.

No proposal should inject scenario names, expected strings or benchmark-specific recipes into a model profile. No stronger-model substitution is recommended. For every proposed change, retain at least one unrelated workflow and both model families as checks, compare complete distributions and actual receipts, and preserve the frozen campaign. The separately activated DocBlocks run can test the missing-capability hypothesis; it cannot prove a general improvement without those broader checks.

reports.activation-correction-001/condition-post:
# Separate DocBlocks activation-condition postmortem

All six trials, automatic CLI judging, declared-artifact inline judging and actual tool/provenance review are complete. This is a separately frozen condition; none of its outcomes replaces a baseline cell.

## Condition and interpretation

The original six baseline trials exposed only 20 filesystem tools, with no DocBlocks capability. This adapter adds the supported binary `expectedDeliverable` at the implementer kickoff, changing the session/tool prompt while preserving the original task wording, fixtures, standard gates, native 0.1.54, Chrome override, generalist auto and three repetitions per model. Each corrected-condition trial exposes 39 tools, including 19 DocBlocks tools. No source, model tuning or gate was edited. [Condition](condition.json), [adapter](cli.ts), [baseline identity check](baseline-identity-check.json).

Raw outcomes are Qwen 2/3 and Gemma 0/3. The activation hypothesis is supported: both models actually call production DocBlocks tools, and Qwen produces saved branded decks in all three attempts. The adapter is not a complete repair fix. Its binary messageGezel repair request is rejected by the existing ad-hoc handoff boundary before reaching the model. Failed repair therefore cannot be interpreted as a model ignoring feedback, and these results are not a clean comparison under fully working repair.

## Each recorded trial

| Model / repetition | Raw result | Capability | Whole trial | Inline mean | CLI mean | Saved report / PPTX |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| gemma / 1 | fail | 2.0 | 356.8 s | noArtifact | noArtifact | 0 / 0 |
| gemma / 2 | fail | 2.8 | 405.7 s | noArtifact | noArtifact | 0 / 0 |
| gemma / 3 | fail | 3.5 | 363.9 s | noArtifact | noArtifact | 0 / 0 |
| qwen / 1 | pass | 9.5 | 130.1 s | 5.0 | 8.0 | 1 / 1 |
| qwen / 2 | fail | 6.4 | 418.2 s | 5.3 | 6.3 | 1 / 1 |
| qwen / 3 | pass | 9.5 | 111.6 s | 6.0 | 5.7 | 1 / 1 |

Missing declared reports receive no qualitative score, not a fabricated zero. Scores apply to the Markdown reports under the original grounding/candor/usefulness axes; saved binary provenance is reviewed separately. All original judgments are retained. [Inline detail](inline-judge-report.md), [CLI ledger](advisory-judge-report.json).

## Evidence-based failures and remaining limitations

- Qwen r1 and r3 successfully infer, apply, convert, save, inspect and compare. Their reports reproduce the correct theme and four slides. R1 omits timing/accessibility degradation; r3 includes it. Both attribute the low text-similarity figure to word-count growth without establishing that causal explanation. R3 suggests a visual/font check but does not resolve the degraded categories.
- Qwen r2 uses `apply_inferred_theme` and produces the branded deck and a report, but never calls the separately required `infer_theme_from_file`. Its frozen gate stops at 8/9. It is a provenance-step miss, not absent DocBlocks capability; the repair nudge is rejected before model delivery. The report omits two degraded comparison categories.
- Gemma r1/r2 successfully infer/apply/convert/inspect/compare, but fail `save_artifact` destination validation. R1 alternates a string destination and an incomplete object; r2 additionally puts `expectedSha256` at the wrong level. These are concrete initial schema errors. R2 also attempts to write a report, but the grounding guard rejects it; neither declares a saved report or deck. The unavailable repair is a separate limitation.
- The evidence guard rejects several facts already returned by DocBlocks, demanding `read_file` evidence instead. Qwen recovers through additional reads/citations; some final citation labels are inaccurate. Gemma encounters the same boundary. This demonstrates a tool-receipt integration gap; it does not justify overlooking genuinely unsupported explanations.
- The frozen grounding rubric calls colors beyond its short list fabrication, but inference actually returns three additional palette colors. R1 Qwen includes these tool-supported colors. This inconsistency is disclosed rather than claiming those colors were invented.

Gemma r3 repeats three save-destination validation failures and a report-write rejection despite successful infer/apply/convert/inspect/compare calls. Its final apology correctly acknowledges that neither requested file was saved. Its claim that the supplied save schema specified a string is not independently established by the saved tool-surface log; schema compaction is enabled, but the complete served schema was not captured for this audit. The observed argument errors are established, while their attribution solely to model understanding is qualified. [Full evidence](evidence-review.json) retains exact tool failures, model-facing surfaces, saved-file hashes and comparison responses.

## Performance in this condition

All three attempts per model, including failed repair waits, are included. These measurements do not replace the baseline distributions. Native throughput does not measure final-deliverable completion.

| Median metric | Qwen | Gemma |
|---|---:|---:|
| Whole trial (s) | 130.1 | 363.9 |
| Decode tokens/s | 55.7 | 118.9 |
| Prefill tokens/s | 780.5 | 1,199.9 |
| First model-turn TTFT (s) | 36.4 | 13.7 |
| Process peak RSS (MB) | 22,657.0 | 17,640.0 |
| Host peak used RAM (MB) | 47,718.0 | 41,596.0 |
| GPU peak used memory (MB) | 29,168.0 | 15,039.0 |

GPU coverage: Qwen 3/3, Gemma 3/3. [Machine-readable performance](review-statistics.json) retains denominators.

## Next experiment

Preserve binary activation through a repair path accepted by `packages/service/src/chat/manager.ts`, integrate DocBlocks read/inspection receipts into `evidence-ledger.ts`, and surface a compact schema-valid save destination without weakening permissions. Test those shared contracts on a DOCX publication task as well as a PPTX task with both families. Keep the new condition separately versioned; do not launch extra inference or retroactively replace this completed experiment.
